### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. epidermolysis bullosa simplex 1B, generalized intermediate  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.740)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-446107, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567, Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-9725554, Reactome:R-HSA-9927432)

**Proposed mechanism:** KRT14 (HGNC:6416) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal keratinization (HP:0011331); Abnormal keratinization (HP:0011331) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin morphology (HP:0001700); Abnormal skin morphology (HP:0001700) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermal fragility (HP:0007327); Abnormal skin morphology (HP:0001700) —LEADS_TO→ Reticulated hyperpigmentation of skin (HP:0033738). Mutations in KRT14 disrupt keratin intermediate filament network formation and keratinization, leading to compromised epidermal structure and function, manifesting as abnormal skin morphology, epidermal fragility, and reticulated hyperpigmentation.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in KRT14 with a consistent loss-of-function effect in both disease types would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if variants in KRT14 associated with one disease consistently show a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect while the other shows loss-of-function, this hypothesis would be falsified.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in KRT14 provides a common target for therapeutic strategies aimed at stabilizing keratin structure or improving keratinocyte function in both dermatopathia pigmentosa reticularis and epidermolysis bullosa simplex.

#### 2. epidermolysis bullosa simplex 1A, generalized severe  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.735)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-446107, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567, Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-9725554, Reactome:R-HSA-9927432)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in KRT14 (null) —DISRUPTS→ KRT14 (HGNC:6416); KRT14 (HGNC:6416) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal keratin filament organization (HP:0003690); Abnormal keratin filament organization (HP:0003690) —LEADS_TO→ Skin fragility (HP:0007257); Abnormal keratin filament organization (HP:0003690) —LEADS_TO→ Reticulated hyperpigmentation (HP:0011707); Skin fragility (HP:0007257) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex 1A, generalized severe (MONDO:0007550); Reticulated hyperpigmentation (HP:0011707) —LEADS_TO→ Dermatopathia pigmentosa reticularis (MONDO:0007445). Pathogenic variants in KRT14 lead to abnormal keratin filament organization, which in turn causes skin fragility and reticulated hyperpigmentation. Skin fragility is the primary phenotype in epidermolysis bullosa simplex 1A, generalized severe, while the combination of skin fragility and reticulated hyperpigmentation defines dermatopathia pigmentosa reticularis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic KRT14 variants in individuals with dermatopathia pigmentosa reticularis that do not affect keratin filament organization or skin fragility, or conversely, identification of pathogenic variants in KRT14 for epidermolysis bullosa simplex 1A, generalized severe, that do not impact keratin network integrity. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of KRT14 in these distinct but related dermatological conditions could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting keratin filament stability or downstream pathways affected by its dysfunction, potentially benefiting patients with either disease.
